heading: Hastings' area law for gapped one-dimensional ground states
lede: Hastings' 2007 argument for the one-dimensional area law and polynomial matrix product state approximation is now fully proved and verified locally in Lean, with one common Lieb–Robinson pair throughout. The new contributions have been submitted for review; local verification and merged coverage are distinguished below. The proof factors the ground-state projector near a cut and uses the resulting mutual-information gain to bound the entanglement entropy independently of chain length.
description: Hastings' one-dimensional area law in Lean 4: verified proofs, review status and corrections to the printed argument.

routes.heading: How Hastings proves the area law
routes.intro: The chain has N sites of local dimension D, interaction terms of norm at most J, and a unique ground state Ψ0 with gap ΔE. The paper chooses a Lieb–Robinson velocity v and decay length ξC, then sets ξ = max(2v/ΔE, ξC) and ξ′ = 6ξ. The verified proofs use one common choice throughout: v = 40cRJ, ξC = 80, and s = max(80cRJ/ΔE, 80), with ξ′ = 6s. Here cR depends only on the interaction range R, and is numerical for nearest-neighbour interactions. The commutator bound has numerical prefactor 4 times the size of the first support and permits an arbitrary finite second support. For J > 0 this gives exactly the paper's interaction-proportional velocity; the zero-interaction case is included in the entropy and approximation statements. Both contraction and positive semidefinite factorizations have error ε(l) = K s3e−l/(6s), with K depending only on R. No restriction on identifying the source parameters remains.

stages.title: Approximate factorization of the ground-state projector
stages.physics: Fix a cut between sites j and j + 1 and a length l. Lemma 1 constructs three contractions: OL acting left of the cut, OR acting right of it, and OB acting on the window of 2l sites around it. Their product approximates the projector P0 onto Ψ0 in operator norm. The construction splits H into left, buffer and right parts, centres each at the ground state, and averages each against a Gaussian under time evolution. The gap makes these averages nearly annihilate Ψ0; the Lieb–Robinson bound makes them nearly local. Spectral cutoffs of the localized left and right parts give orthogonal projections OL, OR. A localized Gaussian average in the interaction picture gives the window contraction. This first window factor need not be positive. Lemma 4 replaces it by OB†OB, which is positive semidefinite; the constructed factors can have kernels.
stages.delivers: At an original fixed localization length, the Gaussian construction retains a square-root prefactor, and making the window factor positive also incurs a square-root loss in the error. The common admissible source length s absorbs both losses: the contraction and positive semidefinite versions each satisfy ‖OBOLOR − P0‖ ≤ K s3e−l/(6s). Thus the source rate ξ′ = 6s holds with a polynomial factorization constant, uniformly in the chain length, the cut and the local dimension. The fixed-length corrections remain recorded in the paper-gap notes.

stages.title: The bootstrap: entropy from overlap with low Schmidt rank
stages.physics: Suppose a mixture ρ of states of Schmidt rank at most k across the cut has overlap P with the ground state. Applying the factorization at window length m multiplies the Schmidt rank by at most D2m, since OB acts on 2m sites, and leaves a state close to Ψ0. By the variational characterization of the Schmidt coefficients, the weight of Ψ0 beyond its first k D2m Schmidt coefficients is then at most 2C12e−2m/ξ′/P for every m. Maximizing the entropy subject to this whole family of geometric tail constraints bounds the entropy of the half chain.
stages.delivers: Lemma 2: S(ρ01,j) ≤ ln k + ξ′ ln(2C12/P) ln D + F(ξ′, D), with F(ξ′, D) = (ξ′ + 4) ln D + 1 + ln(D2 − 1) + ln(ξ′/2 + 1), proved for gapped chains at ξ′ = 6s with C1 = K s3. The paper notes that the argument extends to the Rényi entropies Sα whenever e−2α/ξ′(D2)1−α < 1. This is proved for 0 < α < 1, with 4 ln D − ln(1 − (D2)1−αe−2α/ξ′)/(1 − α) in place of F, and for α > 1, where Sα ≤ S gives the bound with F itself.

stages.title: Mutual information across a cut
stages.physics: Assume that the high-entropy hypothesis and the bootstrap give p = Tr(P0σ) ≤ 2ε, where σ is the product of the two half-chain marginals. The window effect is E = OB†OB, as in the note added to the paper; OLOR supplies an auxiliary projection, not the measurement on the window. On the ground state, the expectation of E is at least 1 − 4ε. On σ it is at most 20ε when ε ≤ 1/136. Set η = 2ε. A measurement cannot increase relative entropy, and relative entropy with respect to the product of the marginals is mutual information. The resulting binary relative entropy gives the lower bound below; nonnegativity handles larger η.
stages.delivers: Under this overlap hypothesis, the mutual information of the two halves of the window is at least (1 − 2η(l)) l/ξ′ − ln(2C1) − 7, where η(l) = 2C1e−l/ξ′ and 4C1 > 1. This retains the exponential rate without replacing the window factor in the factorization by its positive repair, and it is proved for the ground state of a gapped chain at the common source length ξ′ = 6s, with the constants of Lemma 1 above. It is a conditional step in the high-entropy contradiction, not a lower bound for every gapped ground state.

stages.title: The doubling argument
stages.physics: Suppose some half chain had entropy above a large value Smax. Then the entropy stays above 2Smax/3 along a whole window of length l0 of order Smax/ln D. Let Sl be the largest entropy of an interval of length l in that window. Subadditivity alone gives S2l ≤ 2Sl; combining the bootstrap with the mutual-information bound sharpens this to S2l ≤ 2Sl − (1 − 4C1e−l/ξ′) l/ξ′ + ln(2C1) + 7. Each doubling therefore lowers the entropy per site by a fixed amount, while it starts at most at ln D and can never become negative. Only a bounded number of doublings fit, which bounds l0, contradicting the choice of Smax.
stages.delivers: For every cut i, the verified theorem gives the printed form S(ρ01,i) ≤ Smax = c0 ξ′ ln ξ′ ln D · 2ξ′ ln D, with ξ′ = 6s and c0 depending only on the interaction range. For nearest-neighbour interactions it is numerical. At the original fixed length the corrected doubling iteration gives 4 raised to ξ′ ln D; choosing the common admissible source length absorbs this loss and recovers the printed form. The bound is uniform in the cut and chain length and exponential in J/ΔE. The neighbouring one-dimensional proof gives a constant linear in 1 + J/Δ.

routes.heading: Matrix product states and correlations
routes.intro: The same factorization controls more than the entropy. It bounds the small Schmidt coefficients that a matrix product state approximation discards, and it limits how strongly an operator far from a cut can correlate with an operator diagonal in the Schmidt basis of that cut.

stages.title: Decay of the Schmidt coefficients and matrix product states
stages.physics: Order the Schmidt coefficients of Ψ0 across a cut by size. The first k0 = e2S/2 of them carry weight at least one half, where S is the entropy of the half chain, so the bootstrap applies with P = 1/2 and bounds the weight beyond k0D2m by 4C12e−2m/ξ′. Rewritten in terms of the number k′ of coefficients kept, the discarded weight decays like a power of k′/k0. Truncating every cut of the chain to k′ Schmidt vectors then gives a matrix product state of bond dimension k′. The paper's construction assumes a uniform entropy bound; on the whole chain one integer k0 at least exp(2S)/2 at every cut serves as the truncation threshold. For a gapped chain the area law supplies it, as k0 = ⌈exp(2Smax)/2⌉, and Lemma 1 supplies the factorization, both with constants independent of the chain length.
stages.delivers: The Schmidt weight beyond the first k′ coefficients is at most 4C12 e2/ξ′ (k′/k0)−1/(ξ′ ln D), so sequential truncation gives an unnormalized matrix product vector Φ of bond dimension at most k′ with squared Hilbert-space error ‖Φ − Ψ0‖² of order (N − 1) (k′/k0)−1/(ξ′ ln D). This is proved for gapped chains, at ξ′ = 6s, with k0 = ⌈exp(2Smax)/2⌉ taken from the printed entropy bound and independent of the chain length. The norm error is the square root of this bound. For fixed chain parameters, polynomial bond dimension therefore gives polynomial accuracy. For N < 2 no cut is truncated and Φ = Ψ0; the displayed power-law expression is used for N ≥ 2.

stages.title: Correlations of Schmidt-diagonal operators
stages.physics: An operator BL acting on the left half and diagonal in the Schmidt basis of Ψ0 has a mirror image BR on the right half with BLΨ0 = BRΨ0. Let A act at distance at least l from the cut. Each factor of the approximate factorization nearly fixes Ψ0 and commutes with one of A, BL, BR by its support, so a chain of triangle inequalities moves BL past A at a small cost. Hastings uses this to show that certain expander matrix product states, whose correlations of this kind stay large, are not ground states of gapped chains.
stages.delivers: Lemma 3: |⟨Ψ0, ABL Ψ0⟩ − ⟨Ψ0, A Ψ0⟩⟨Ψ0, BL Ψ0⟩| ≤ 3√(2ε(l)) + ε(l) for contractions A and BL. The proof uses the positive semidefinite factorization at the same source length, with ε(l) = K s3e−l/(6s). The positive repair halves the rate at a fixed auxiliary length, but the common enlarged length s absorbs that loss. No additional hypothesis on the gapped chain is introduced.

glossary: S(ρ<sub>1,i</sub>) = −Tr ρ log ρ for the reduced density matrix ρ of the ground state on the first i sites, measuring the entanglement across the cut after site i.
The ground state Ψ<sub>0</sub> is unique and every other eigenvalue of H exceeds the ground energy by at least ΔE.
A bound on how far, in a given time, the evolution under a local Hamiltonian can spread an operator acting on a few sites; on a chain it holds with a velocity v and a decay length ξ<sub>C</sub>.

A product O<sub>B</sub>O<sub>L</sub>O<sub>R</sub> approximating the ground-state projector in operator norm. The left and right factors are orthogonal projections. The window factor can be a contraction or a positive semidefinite contraction. The latter incurs a square-root loss at a fixed localization length; enlarging the admissible source length gives both forms the same rate ξ′ = 6s.
The number of nonzero terms in the Schmidt decomposition of a vector across a cut, that is, the rank of the reduced density matrix of either side.
An operator on one side of a cut that is diagonal in the Schmidt basis of the ground state across that cut.
I(X : Y) = S(X) + S(Y) − S(X ∪ Y), the relative entropy of the state on X ∪ Y to the product of its marginals.
Relative entropy cannot increase under a quantum channel, in particular under a measurement.

A vector on a chain written as a contraction of one tensor per site, with open ends. Every internal Schmidt rank is at most the corresponding bond dimension. For a nonzero vector on a chain of at least two sites, the minimal possible maximal bond dimension equals the largest Schmidt rank across internal cuts; an arbitrary representation may have larger bonds.
